**This line is one of the paid layer campaign that [#1659](https://github.com/headwater-ai/headwater/issues/1659) asked for.** `tools/probe/campaign.sh` recorded it as line 1 of the plan of batch B, a plan that draws its lines from `tools/probe/layer-campaign.spec`. It is the present arm of the campaign tier over the discovery selection, at 118 repetitions per probe, on `claude-sonnet-5` under Claude Code 2.1.288 with a cap of 80 turns for each session. The line leaves out `HW-PROBE-the-authoring-skill-reaches-an-agent-that-is-about-to-write-a-governed-document`, because no arm without `.claude/` can satisfy it.

**One tree.** Every session ran in a fresh copy of a `git archive` of commit `debe0c70`, with the engine of that commit. Batch B ran after batch A on the same pin that batch A ended on.

**What the recorder counted.** The line holds 354 sessions and cost 13743 cents. The intent hook was live in 354 of them. None stopped at the turn cap, and none at the session budget. The recorder reports 21 paths outside the workspace named in a call of this line, 0 sessions uncounted, and 0 web-tool calls.

**The contract of this batch.** The sessions ran under the recorder contract of spec 15: a `bwrap` sandbox with no network of its own, an empty configuration directory, `--setting-sources project,local`, the permission mode `dontAsk`, and `WebSearch` and `WebFetch` denied. The batches of 2026-09-28 and 2026-09-30 ran under `bypassPermissions` and the configuration of the host, so a rate from this batch does not compare with a rate from those batches.

**Where the figures are.** The rates, the intervals and the comparisons of this line are in the generated result that reads this transcript, and this document states none of them.

Good examples to read in full:\\n   - `engine/crates/check/src/retired.rs` (the retired-term rule, implementation)\\n   - `engine/crates/check/src/shape.rs` and `engine/crates/check/src/anchors.rs` (other rule implementations, for pattern/style)\\n   - `.headwater/packages/headwater-standard/taxonomy.yml` (where rules are declared, incl. severity: error vs advisory)\\n   - `.headwater/overlay.yml` (project-level rule config, e.g. `retired_terms` list — read the CLAUDE.md section \\\"What a check does with these rules\\\" for the error-vs-advisory distinction: error = mechanical total remedy, advisory = remedy is a rewrite)\\n   - The check crate's rule registry/dispatch (find where rules are registered/listed so a new rule actually gets invoked — grep for how `retired.rs`'s rule is wired into `engine/crates/check/src/lib.rs` or similar)\\n   - Existing acceptance-criteria docs under `docs/acceptance-criteria/` for a similar rule, and any `docs/decisions/` or `docs/spec/` entries that define what \\\"declared\\\" vs \\\"implemented\\\" means in this repo's own vocabulary\\n   - Test fixtures pattern: `engine/crates/check/fixtures/*.taxonomy.yml` and `engine/crates/check/fixtures/check.report`, and the corresponding test file (e.g. `engine/crates/check/tests/outside_root.rs` or similar) so you can add a fixture + test for the new rule the same way.\\n\\n## What \\\"empty summary\\\" means here\\n\\nFind the taxonomy's canonical name for a document's summary field (grep front matter / metadata schema for \\\"summary\\\" across `.headwater/` and `docs/spec/` — there may be a `docs/spec/` part describing document front matter fields). Determine whether \\\"empty\\\" should mean the field is absent entirely, or present but blank/whitespace-only — handle both.\\n\\n## Decide severity\\n\\nPer CLAUDE.md: \\\"A rule is an error when its remedy is mechanical and total... A rule is advisory when the remedy is a rewrite.\\\" Writing a summary is a rewrite (requires judgment, not a mechanical fix `--fix` could derive), so this should almost certainly be `advisory`, matching the pattern of other advisory, rewrite-remedy rules (e.g. sentence length, stock metaphors). Confirm this against how other similarly-judgmental rules are classified in `.headwater/packages/headwater-standard/taxonomy.yml`, and use that classification consistently. Do not mark it `error` unless you find a strong reason in the taxonomy's own rules for doing so.\\n\\n## Implementation requirements\\n\\n1. Declare the rule in the taxonomy (likely `.headwater/packages/headwater-standard/taxonomy.yml`, possibly with a project-level override/addition in `.headwater/overlay.yml` — follow whatever the existing rules do; some rules may be declared entirely in one package file). Give it a clear rule identifier following this repo's naming convention (e.g. something like `language.summary.empty` or whatever namespace existing rules use — check the convention from `retired_terms`'s rule id).\\n2. Implement the check in the Rust engine (new file or added function in `engine/crates/check/src/`, following the style of `retired.rs`), and wire it into the rule dispatch/registry so `headwater check` actually runs it.\\n3. Add a test fixture and a test, following the existing fixture pattern (a `.taxonomy.yml` fixture plus a report fixture, or whatever pattern the existing tests for `retired.rs`/`shape.rs` use).\\n4. Build the engine using the exact command from CLAUDE.md: `cargo build --profile dev-release -p headwater-cli --manifest-path engine/Cargo.toml --locked` (never `--release`). Run the relevant test suite (`cargo test` scoped to the check crate) and confirm it passes.\\n5. Run `headwater check` (the built binary) against this repo itself to sanity-check the new rule doesn't crash and produces sane output. Do NOT run `--fix` destructively without checking first what it would change; if it would modify files, just report what it would do rather than applying it, unless the change is obviously just this feature's own fixtures.\\n\\n## Do NOT do\\n\\n- Do not attempt git operations of any kind (this is not a git repo).\\n- Do not create any document under `docs/` via a raw Write (CLAUDE.md says a hook refuses that for new docs) — if you need a new `docs/acceptance-criteria/` entry, use the `headwater-authoring` skill or `headwater new` CLI verb, not a raw file write. If this is optional/out of scope, skip writing a new acceptance-criteria doc rather than fighting the hook, and just focus on the taxonomy declaration + engine implementation + tests.\\n- Do not refactor unrelated code.\\n\\n## What to report back (be specific, with file paths and line numbers)\\n\\n1. Where exactly the rule is declared (file + the rule's identifier/key as declared).\\n2. Where exactly the rule is implemented (file + function/struct name).\\n3. What severity it was given, and the one-sentence justification tying it to CLAUDE.md's error-vs-advisory distinction.\\n4. What you built/tested and whether it passed.\\n5. Any fixtures or files you added or edited, as a list.\"}"

Taxonomy declaration pattern (`.headwater/packages/headwater-standard/taxonomy.yml`)\\n   - Facets are declared under `facets:` (e.g. `summary` at lines 381-385: `role: scent`, `type: string`, `required: true`, `volatility: mutable`).\\n   - Obligations are declared under `obligations:` (~line 554+), each with `statement`, `rationale`, `class`, `prevents`, and `severity: high|medium|low` (the OBLIGATION's severity scale, not the check's). Example, `CT-FACET-3` (lines 1285-1295):\\n     ```yaml\\n     CT-FACET-3:\\n       mechanism: check:facet.value.blank\\n       discharges: [OB-FACET-3]\\n       trigger: pull_request\\n       posture: advisory\\n       acts: detective\\n       promotion:\\n         criteria:\\n           window: one release of the taxonomy over an adopting corpus\\n           threshold: no false positive, because the rule reads the core schema's own null resolver and an empty scalar rather than deciding what blank means\\n           sample: every finding of one run over the adopting corpus, adjudicated once\\n     ```\\n   - Also see `CT-LANG-3` (line 1233) → `mechanism: check:language.retired_term.used` as another posture:advisory example, same shape.\\n\\n2. Severity is split across TWO axes, and this is explicit doctrine — read `engine/crates/check/src/finding.rs:22-29` (comment) and `docs/spec/12-check-layer.md#severity-is-the-checks-posture-is-the-controls`:\\n   - The CHECK (Rust code) reports `Severity::Error|Warn|Info` (finding.rs:54-62) — this is set in the Rust `Finding` literal, e.g. `severity: Severity::Error`.\\n   - The OBLIGATION (taxonomy) carries `severity: high|medium|low` — how much the invariant matters.\\n   - Whether a finding BLOCKS is the CONTROL's `posture: advisory|blocking` field, not the check's severity. So \\\"error vs advisory\\\" in your framing maps to: Rust-side `Severity::Error` (always, for a hard content defect) + taxonomy-side `posture: advisory` (because promotion criteria haven't been met yet — nearly every existing rule in this taxonomy is `posture: advisory`; only a handful are `blocking`, e.g. lines ~1355, 1365, 1375).\\n\\n3. Rust implementation / registry mechanics:\\n   - Rule ID → Rust mapping has NO match statement or macro dispatch by string; each rule is its own module in `engine/crates/check/src/`, exposing `pub const RULE: &str = \\\"the.dotted.id\\\"` that must exactly match the taxonomy's `mechanism: check:<id>` suffix. ~48 such modules exist (list in `engine/crates/check/src/lib.rs:233-...`, `pub const RULES: [&str; 48] = [facet_required::RULE, facet_value::RULE, facet_blank::RULE, ...]`).\\n   - Each rule struct implements the `DocumentCheck` trait (`crate::scope::DocumentCheck`): `const RULE`, `const VERSION: u32` (cache-busting), `const EXPORTABLE_AS: ExportTargets`, `fn instantiates(&self, kind: &str) -> bool`, `fn evaluate(&self, view: &DocumentView<'_>) -> Outcome`.\\n   - \\\"Shape-origin\\\" checks (like this one) are GENERATED from taxonomy declarations via a `::over(shape: &Shape) -> Self` constructor that reads `Shape` (facets/kinds) rather than hardcoding names — no per-facet code needed.\\n   - The `obligation` field of `Finding` is left `None` in the check code itself; the runtime binds rule→obligation later via the control's `discharges`, through `crate::register` (see finding.rs:12-19).\\n\\n4. Exact analog for \\\"field is empty\\\" — `engine/crates/check/src/facet_blank.rs` (176 lines), rule id `facet.value.blank`, struct `Blank`, generated `over(shape)` over every facet declared `type: string`, not forbidden by the kind. In `evaluate()` (lines 169-214) it reads `view.facets().entry(facet)`, calls `headwater_yaml::core_schema::as_null(scalar)` to catch `title:`/`title: ~`/`title: null`, and separately checks `scalar.text.trim().is_empty()` for `title: \\\"\\\"`. Always emits `severity: Severity::Error`, `obligation: None`, `patch: None` (no mechanical fix — \\\"the value...is a name somebody has to write\\\"). Companion `facet_required.rs` (129 lines) is the \\\"missing key entirely\\\" rule (`facet.required.missing`), same shape, `line: 0` since there's no line for an absent key.\\n   - Since `summary` is already `type: string`, `facet_blank.rs` ALREADY instantiates over it and already reports a blank summary today, with message `` `summary` is declared with no value `` or `` `summary` is declared as empty text ``.\\n\\n5. Acceptance-criteria docs (`docs/acceptance-criteria/`): only 6 files exist total (5 numbered + README), and they are NOT 1:1 with rule IDs — they're reserved for a handful of subtler engine-behavior claims (e.g. `0002-...-heading.md` for `section.required.missing`, `0003-...` for path-dedup logic). Most of the ~48 rules (including `facet.value.blank` / `facet.required.missing`) have NO acceptance-criteria doc. So a new \\\"summary empty\\\" rule is not expected to require one by convention — only add one if the rule's correctness condition is non-obvious the way the existing 5 are.\\n\\nRecommendation: before writing new code, confirm with the user whether they actually want something `facet.value.blank` doesn't already give them (e.g., a summary-specific message/remediation, or a different severity/posture), since the generic blank-facet rule already covers `summary` structurally.\",\"type\":\"message\",\"recipient\":\"main\",\"content\":\"KEY FINDING FIRST: `summary` is already a `type: …\"}"

Check docs/subsystems/parse-and-census.md — mentions \\\"census outcome\\\".\\n4. Check .headwater/overlay.yml and .gitattributes for \\\"merge=headwater-regenerate\\\" entries — what files are marked as derived folds that need regeneration on merge, and find the document that explains WHY (the design rationale decision document).\\n5. Report its exact path, the document title, and a short quote (1-3 sentences) showing it addresses this scenario. If multiple documents are candidates, report all of them and explain which one is the most precise match (i.e., the one that specifically \\\"rules\\\" on this, as opposed to one that merely mentions it in passing).\"}"
